patches.old:
I.1. He says, “In the first commandment I told you to keep faith, fear and self-control.” “Yes, sir,” I say. “Now I also want to explain their powers,” he says. “Then you can understand the power of each and how each works. Their activities are twofold. They have to do with what is right and what is wrong.”[a]

I.2. “Trust what is right. Do not trust what is wrong. What is right has a straight road. What is wrong has a crooked one. Walk on the straight [and level] road. Leave the crooked one.”[b]

I.3. “The crooked road has no tracks. It has places with no path and many stumbling blocks. It is rough and thorny, so it harms the people who walk on it.”

I.4. “People on the straight road walk smoothly, without stumbling. It is neither rough nor thorny. You see that it is better to travel this road.”

I.5. I say, “Sir, I am pleased to travel this road.” He says, “You will travel it. So will everyone who turns to the Lord with their whole heart.”[c]

II.1. He says, “Now hear about faith. Two angels are with a person: an angel of righteousness and an angel of wickedness.”

II.2. I say, “Sir, how can I recognize what each does, since both angels live with me?”

II.3. “Listen and understand them,” he says. “The angel of righteousness is tender, modest, gentle and quiet. When he rises up in your heart, he speaks with you at once about righteousness, purity, dignity, contentment, every right deed and every glorious virtue. When these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of righteousness is with you. [These are the works of the angel of righteousness.] Trust him and his works.”[d]

II.4. “Now look at what the angel of wickedness does. He is quick-tempered, bitter and senseless. His works are evil and overthrow God’s servants. When he rises up in your heart, recognize him by what he does.”[e]

II.5. I say, “Sir, I do not know how to recognize him.” “Listen,” he says. “When quick temper or bitterness comes over you, know that he is in you. Then come cravings for many undertakings, costly foods and intoxicating drinks, many revelries, all kinds of luxuries and things that are not fitting. There are also desire for women, greed, haughtiness, boastfulness and other things like these. When these things rise up in your heart, know that the angel of wickedness is with you.”[f]

II.6. “When you recognize his works, leave him and put no trust in him. His works are evil and do no good for God’s servants. You know what both angels do. Discern their activities and trust the angel of righteousness.”

II.7. “Leave the angel of wickedness. His teaching is evil in every deed. If someone is faithful and this angel’s thought rises up in their heart, that man or woman must commit some sin.”[g]

II.8. “Again, a man or woman may be very wicked. If the works of the angel of righteousness rise up in their heart, they must necessarily do something good.”[g]

II.9. He says, “You see that it is good to follow the angel of righteousness and renounce the angel of wickedness.”

II.10. “This commandment explains faith. Trust the works of the angel of righteousness. By doing them, you will live to God. Believe that the works of the angel of wickedness are grievous. By not doing them, you will live to God.”[h]

patches.reason: In II.4, πρῶτον πάντων explicitly supplies “First of all.” In II.5, πολυτέλεια names extravagance, not merely costly foods, and ἐδεσμάτων πολλῶν specifies many foods. Restore both omitted elements while preserving the separate undertakings and revelries items. Reconsideration of prior lexical implementation: replace “costly foods” with the already recorded choice “extravagance,” without changing that lexical decision. All paragraph prefixes, divisions, markers, servant terminology and necessity claims remain unchanged.

patches.old: At ii.5 physical343 the print and Lake’s transcription read quick temper OR bitterness; the raw transcription’s nominative article hē was an error for the conjunction ē and is corrected to match the print. The complete Greek vice list is retained, including luxuries of various kinds AND things that are not fitting, preserving the earlier grammatical decision. The printed Vulgata list at49 differs and lacks several Greek items; Palatina printed95 is closer but not identical. Latin differences are not silently harmonized into the Greek.
